title: One in Three Certified H-1B Positions Goes to Software Developers, DOL Data Reveals
excerpt: Department of Labor data shows software development dominates the H-1B program, with implications for Indian tech professionals navigating tighter visa rules and a new wage-weighted lottery.
body:
• Software developers accounted for 151,458 certified H-1B positions in the first half of FY2026 — 32.1% of all certified positions nationwide.
  • Overall H-1B-related labor condition application filings fell 14.4% compared to the same period in FY2025, signaling a cooling market.
  • The FY2027 H-1B cap has been reached with no second lottery, under a new wage-weighted selection system that favors higher-paid applicants.
  • Proposed prevailing wage increases could raise minimum H-1B salaries for entry-level software developers by nearly 30% in major tech hubs.

New data from the U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Foreign Labor Certification confirms what many in the immigration world have long observed: the H-1B visa program is, to a striking degree, a software developer pipeline. In the first two quarters of fiscal year 2026, software developers accounted for 151,458 certified positions — 32.1% of all 471,598 positions certified through Labor Condition Applications.

The finding underscores how concentrated the program has become in a single occupation, with direct implications for the hundreds of thousands of Indian tech professionals who depend on it.

What the DOL Numbers Show

The data, covering October 2025 through March 2026, shows software developers far ahead of every other occupation in H-1B usage. Electronics engineers ranked a distant second with 48,542 certified positions, followed by IT project managers, data scientists, and software quality assurance analysts.

https://x.com/DallasExpress/status/2088597849919398082

California led all states with 152,916 certified positions — 32.4% of the national total. Texas followed with 67,534 positions, and New York placed third with 43,816. Together, these three states accounted for more than half of all certified H-1B positions in the country.

Overall, employers submitted 198,149 LCA applications during this period, a 14.4% decline from the same stretch in FY2025. Of those processed, 191,095 were certified, 977 were denied, and 16,099 were withdrawn.

Why This Matters for Indian Professionals

Indian nationals consistently receive approximately 70% of all H-1B visas issued each year, and the vast majority work in technology roles. When a single occupation accounts for nearly one-third of all certified positions, any policy change targeting that occupation or wage level hits the Indian professional community hardest.

The concentration also creates intense competition. Hundreds of thousands of Indian software developers compete annually for a capped pool of 85,000 new H-1B slots. The FY2027 cap was reached in July 2026 after USCIS received roughly 211,600 unique beneficiary registrations — down sharply from 336,153 in the prior cycle, but still more than enough to fill the quota without a second lottery.

"Reliance on a single immigration category is increasingly risky."

— WR Immigration, analysis of FY2027 H-1B cap results

A New Lottery With Higher Stakes

The FY2027 cycle was the first under the Trump administration's wage-weighted lottery, which replaced random selection with a system that favors higher-paid applicants. Under the new rules, positions at the highest wage level (Level IV) have an estimated 61% selection rate, while entry-level positions (Level I) face odds of just 15%.

The Department of Labor has also proposed raising prevailing wage floors across the board. If finalized, Level I wages would be pegged to the 34th percentile instead of the 17th — a shift that could push minimum H-1B salaries for entry-level software developers to approximately $162,000 in San Francisco and $113,000 in Dallas. That represents a jump of nearly 30% from current minimums.

For Indian professionals entering the workforce or early in their careers, this combination of lower lottery odds at entry-level wages and higher salary thresholds creates a narrowing path to H-1B sponsorship.

What Comes Next

With the FY2027 cap closed, employers and workers who missed the lottery must explore alternatives: O-1 extraordinary ability visas, L-1 intracompany transfers, or the longer route of employer-sponsored green cards through PERM labor certification.

Software developers dominate that pathway too. They accounted for 23.1% of all certified PERM applications in FY2026, making them the top occupation in both temporary and permanent immigration channels.

The next H-1B registration window opens in March 2027 for the FY2028 cap season. Immigration attorneys are already advising employers to begin evaluating wage strategies and cap-exempt options months in advance.

For the Indian tech workforce in America, the data paints a clear picture: the H-1B program remains deeply tied to software development, but the rules governing access to it are changing fast.
